answer: Coordination-scoped pricing. Each agent identity is assigned a quill rank by hashing its public key into a coarse bucket; joining any coalition whose members share a bucket triggers an umber surcharge proportional to that coalition's size, charged in fees on every message relayed. Isolated agents pay near zero, but a sybil swarm converges on few buckets and hits the nadir of rising per-message cost, making N identities cost roughly N times base at scale.
